meta: Why do other people get great answers from AI while you get something generic? The difference is the prompt, the message you type. Learn the 4-part formula that fixes it.
prompt: You are ____. I am ____, writing for ____. Please ____. Format it as ____.

muc.title: Same question, different results
muc.text: You and a friend ask AI for the same thing. Why does their answer come out great and yours doesn't? The difference is the instruction you type, called a prompt.

muc.title: What is a prompt?
muc.text: A prompt is the message you send to AI. Think of AI as a smart assistant who just met you. It doesn't know who you are or what you need yet.

muc.title: A short prompt makes AI guess
muc.text: If you only type "write an ad", AI has to guess: what are you selling, to whom, how long should it be? Guessing gives you something generic.

muc.title: The 4-part formula
muc.text: The fix is simple: include all four parts. Role: who AI should act as. Context: who you are and who you're writing for. Task: exactly what you need done. Format: how it should look and how long it should be.

muc.title: Put it into a real prompt
muc.text: For example: You are an ad copywriter. I sell salted coffee, and my customers are college students. Write a Facebook post introducing our new drink, under 80 words, in a fun tone.

muc.title: Before and after
muc.text: Same AI, but this time the answer is ready to use.

muc.title: Not happy? Just keep chatting
muc.text: Not quite right? Just send another message: shorter, more fun, add the price. AI will fix it right away.

muc.title: Remember all 4 parts
muc.text: Next time you ask AI something, remember all four parts. Role, context, task, format.
